name: design-doc
description: Run an assumptions-first architecture design — registers with stable IDs (A#/DQ#/V#), decision-by-question rounds with a recorded escape hatch, a mid-process adversarial review, a library of quantitative components (request paths, load ceilings, number tables) whose estimates are gated on named spikes — and ship the result as an interactive HTML doc that opens on a full-screen summary deck of 3–5 panels (or one poster), draws its system diagram with Mermaid behind a ten-node overview, cites every entry by a human-readable handle, twins every register entry with a plain-English version the reader sees first, carries declared interactive components (what-if, steps, timeline, matrix) plus compiled TSX as the escape hatch, and, behind a deployed key, answers questions and moves the page from a popover and a Cmd-K palette, plus a PDF printed from the same page, written as a humble proposal that explains and asks for feedback rather than sells.
